title: Rollout constraint cookbook and telemetry sampling cheatsheet — 2028-03
content:
Purpose: compact, practical cookbook for releases constrained by capacity, regional quotas, or regulatory quiet windows; paired with a short telemetry-sampling cheatsheet to make post-rollout signal usable without blowing observability budget.

Context and when to use this doc
- This is a field reference for release leads and on-call engineers when a rollout cannot follow the normal ramp due to: temporary GPU shortage, quota limits in a cloud region, customer contract blackout windows, or planned vendor maintenance windows.
- Use when: average token QPS expected > 80% of regional capacity, or when a release interacts with dedicated pools (Dedicated) and you need to avoid noisy telemetry charges.

High-level constraints cookbook (pattern -> when to apply -> quick config)
1) Soft-capacity lanes (preferred)
   - When: short-term capacity pressure but still have headroom for limited ramp.
   - What: break traffic into 3 lanes: 0.5%, 5%, 30% (example) over 24h. Each lane is gated by success/latency.
   - Quick config: route policy with TTL 1h, canary holdback 95th latency < 120ms, error rate < 0.5%. Autoscale disabled for first 6h.

2) Throttle envelope (for quota-limited providers)
   - When: external quota or burst limits (e.g., partner endpoint, private pool with allocation).
   - What: enforce token caps per minute and burst smoothing. Use leaky-bucket at edge.
   - Quick config: set per-route rate-limit to X tokens/min (match procurement cap), enable per-customer circuit-breaker. Implement graceful 429 -> retry-with-backoff for client SDK.

3) Quiet-window respectful rollout (compliance/enterprise customers)
   - When: customer has blackout windows (no config changes) or regional maintenance.
   - What: schedule change to 02:00-04:00 local, but use micro-canary for 48h instead of fast ramp.
   - Quick config: calendar lock in console, explicit approval from account team; reduce rollout step size to <2% increments.

4) Feature gating with fallback model routing
   - When: new model variant might degrade hat-trick prompts; you have an older stable model.
   - What: route by policy: prefer new model for X% but fallback to stable model on latency or safety failures.
   - Quick config: add fallback rule with 1s timeout, enable structured tool-calling logs for A/B evals.

Release checklist (operational) — abbreviated, use as copyable checklist on release day
- Preflight (72–24h):
  - Confirm capacity plan and admit list (owner: release lead).
  - Snapshot current routing and model pins (tag in git infra repo).
  - Wire up smoke endpoints and sampling queries (observability owner).
  - Stakeholder sync: SRE, Product, Solutions Eng, Account Eng (message in slack #release-orchestra).
- 24h:
  - Final canary traffic slice + test harness run (latency, correctness, safety prompts).
  - Update runbook with throttles and expected token burn.
  - Pre-signed rollback PR ready and smoke playbook tested.
- Launch window:
  - Move to lane 1 (very small %). Observe 1h. Run smoke queries.
  - Decision gate: if green, move to lane 2; else rollback to previous pin.
- Post-launch (0–48h):
  - Raise sampling for impacted routes to 10x baseline for first 4h, then ramp down.
  - Run regression evals (prompt-set) and post results in release notes channel.

Telemetry sampling cheatsheet (practical rules)
- Goal: collect enough signal to detect regressions while minimizing ingestion costs.
- Default sampling tiers:
  - Critical routes (inference for enterprise customers, model-change routes): 100% for first 30m, then 10% for 4h, then 1% baseline.
  - High-volume public routes: 0.1% baseline, increase to 1% when changing model weights.
  - Debug traces (full request/response): only on explicit on-call capture; otherwise redact.
- Quick queries to enable in watchlist:
  - 1) p50/p95 latency by route and model_version (last 60m)
  - 2) token burn per minute by region and customer (last 6h)
  - 3) safety classifier hits by model_version (last 24h)
  - 4) error rates (4xx/5xx split) by tier (last 60m)
- Example sampling config (vector-format for ops entry, pasteable):
  - route: /v1/generate -> sample_rate_initial:1.0@30m, thereafter sample_rate:0.1@4h, steady:0.01
  - route: /v1/embeddings -> steady:0.001, on-deploy-burst:0.01@2h

Observability smoke queries (copy/paste)
- Latency guard: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 50, 95) FROM traces WHERE route IN ('generate') AND model LIKE '%gpt%' SINCE 60 MINUTES
- Token burn spike: SELECT sum(tokens) AS tkn FROM requests WHERE region='us-west1' SINCE 15 MINUTES GROUP BY 1m ORDER BY 1m DESC
- Safety regressions: SELECT count(*) FROM safety_events WHERE model_version='v2028-03' GROUP BY severity SINCE 24 HOURS

Fallback and rollback matrix (one page)
- Signal -> Action -> Owner
  - elevated 95th latency by >40% for 30m -> hold rollout, move traffic to stable model -> SRE on-call + release lead
  - error rate >1% sustained 10m -> immediate rollback to pinned model -> release lead + infra
  - token burn > planned cap (billing) -> cap routes to emergency throttle, notify finance -> infra + finance pager
  - safety classifier uptick -> freeze rollout and escalate to safety team -> safety owner (Priya)

Staffing and communication plan (practical)
- Core: release lead (1), infra owner (1), observability (1), product owner (1).
- Backup: two responders to cover nights.
- Comm: use thread in slack #release-orchestra for play-by-play; call #sre if paged.
- Escalation cadence: 0–15m informal sync, 15–45m decision call if not green, >45m escalate to Eng Director.

Calendar sketch (example 5-day ramp for capacity-constrained rollout)
- Day 0 (prep): config PRs merged, preflight done, runbook link posted.
- Day 1 (canary): 0.5% for 2h -> 2% for 6h -> observe overnight at 2%
- Day 2: 2% -> 10% during low-traffic window -> telemetry sampling elevated
- Day 3: 10% -> 30% if healthy -> sample back to baseline after 12h
- Day 4: full ramp (gradual to 100% or planned production target)

Release notes draft (for internal & customer-facing snippets)
- Intro (internal): "This rollout introduces the latency-optimized tokenizer path and model-variant routing for reduced tail latency across short-prompt workflows. Because of temporary quota constraints in eu-west1 we used a constrained ramp plan; telemetry sampling was elevated on critical routes to accelerate signal collection."
- Impact summary (customer-facing): "Non-breaking performance improvement for short prompts. No expected downtime. Customers in eu-west1 may see progressive exposure over 4 days. We will contact large accounts with bespoke timings."
- Known issues: "Under specific long-conversation traces (>800 tokens) we observed a 1–2% increase in p95; mitigation: fallback routing to legacy quantized path."
- Rollback note: "If a rollback is executed, token routing will revert to model pin v2028-02-stable; call the release lead to confirm."

Unresolved questions / follow-ups
- Can we add per-customer soft-capacity reservations in the routing plane? (ticket: RI-4109)
- Audit cost of temporary sampling increases and create monthly budget (owner: observability).
- Verify legal approval for cross-region micro-canaries when customer data residency applies.

Field notes from last constrained rollout (2027-11)
- Staggering by regional low-traffic windows reduced overall failed requests by 30%.
- Elevated sampling at 10x helped detect subtle safety classifier drift within 3 hours; without that we likely would not have caught a prompt-specific regression until 48h.
- Manual intervention was required to disable autoscale on dedicated pools to avoid uneven allocation; action: make this a one-click toggle in console.

Quick copyable commands (ops)
- Revert routing pin: infra-cli routing pin set --model v2028-02-stable --routes generate,chat
- Install elevated sampling: observability-cli sampler apply --route generate --burst 1.0@30m,0.1@4h,0.01
- Emergency throttle: infra-cli quota throttle set --route generate --rate 2000tokens/m --owner @oncall

Appendix: links and artifacts
- Jira: RI-4021 (rollout plan), RI-4109 (per-customer reservations)
- GitHub: infra PR 1189 (routing fallback logic)
- Slack channels: #release-orchestra, #sre, #observability

Notes to self
- Convert this cheatsheet into a one-click template in Console (templated rollout that applies soft-capacity lane, required approvals, and sampling knobs).
- Add a small playbook card for finance to auto-notify if temporary sampling cost > $X/day.
